subject: Clarify notice window & law-enforcement cooperation — Healix (HIPAA)
messages:
From: Sarah Goldstein <sarah.goldstein@healix-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-legal@healix-health.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Notice timelines + LE collaboration — Healix (HIPAA)

Marcus — thanks for the call earlier. Two items we need clarified before finalizing the DPA: 1) The draft says Redwood will notify "without undue delay" — we need a definitive customer-notice window for HIPAA-covered data (we typically require notification to customer within 72 hours of Redwood confirmation of unauthorized access). 2) Our legal team requires explicit language about law-enforcement preservation requests: if Redwood receives a subpoena or preservation order that prevents customer notice, we need a defined process and expected cadence for informing the customer (and for when that hold is lifted).

Can you confirm you can commit to a 72-hour customer notice (subject to lawful holds), and share proposed wording for the LE hold clause? Also please attach SOC 2 report and DPIA summary as evidence.

— Sarah
CISO, Healix Health

-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Goldstein <sarah.goldstein@healix-health.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice timelines + LE collaboration — Healix (HIPAA)

Thanks Sarah — looping in Priya (Legal) and Monica (Security Ops). Short answers up front: we can commit to customer notification within 72 hours of confirming an unauthorized access event for HIPAA-covered data, except where Redwood is legally prohibited from notifying by a valid law-enforcement preservation request or other court order. When such a hold is invoked we will: 1) notify the customer that Redwood has received a legal process that may limit notice (to the extent allowed), 2) provide the customer with the preserving instrument meta (type of order, issuing jurisdiction, date), and 3) regularly update the customer every 7 days on status unless a shorter cadence is requested.

Priya — can you propose contract language that captures the 72-hour commitment while preserving the lawful-hold carve-out? Monica — please attach the SOC 2 redacted report and DPIA summary; Healix asked for evidence.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

-----

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sarah Goldstein <sarah.goldstein@healix-health.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice timelines + LE collaboration — Healix (HIPAA)

Marcus/Sarah — drafted proposed DPA clause below and attached a redline (DPA-redline-proposal.docx). Key points: 1) "72 hours" remains our target for customer notice after Redwood confirms unauthorized access to Protected Health Information (PHI); 2) carve-out for lawful restrictions; 3) explicit commitment to provide metadata about the legal process; 4) periodic status updates while the hold remains in effect; 5) obligation to notify the customer when the hold is lifted and to resume the standard timeline. Proposed text (editable):

"Incident notification. Redwood will notify Customer as soon as practicable and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood confirms an unauthorized access to Customer's Protected Health Information ("PHI"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may delay notification to the extent Redwood is prohibited from providing notice by applicable law, a court order, or a valid law enforcement preservation request. In such cases, Redwood will: (i) notify Customer that Redwood has received legal process that may restrict notice, to the extent Redwood is permitted to do so; (ii) provide, where lawful and not prohibited by the order, details regarding the type of legal process received (e.g., subpoena, preservation order), the issuing authority/jurisdiction, and the date of the instrument; (iii) provide status updates to Customer at least once every seven (7) days while the legal restriction remains in effect or at a different cadence agreed in writing; and (iv) promptly notify Customer when the legal restriction is lifted and resume notifications under this Section."

A couple negotiation notes: - We should avoid language that ties us to a criminal-law standard for when notification can be delayed (that tends to be ambiguous). - Where feasible, we can offer an SLA credit if notification obligations are materially missed (helps commercial teams).

Monica — please confirm the artifacts you will attach.

— Priya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Operational note: when a preservation order arrives we run a standard check for scope (does it reference Redwood logs/metadata vs. customer content), escalate to Legal immediately, and put an account-level hold in our incident tracking tool. We will share a sanitized summary of the legal instrument where permitted. For high-risk PHI incidents we can also offer a joint incident call within 24 hours of customer request.

— Monica
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — the proposed clause looks good. A couple of small asks from our side before we sign: 1) Please add a sentence confirming Redwood will use "commercially reasonable efforts" to notify the Customer sooner than 72 hours where feasible; 2) For the status updates during a lawful hold, can you commit to including the expected next milestone (e.g., next court hearing date or expected lift date) when available? If you can accept those tweaks we'll run the redline through procurement and get this across the finish line. Also, confirming we received the SOC 2 and DPIA attachments — we'll share them internally with our audit team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Sarah
